summary.short: Selected FY2026 NDAA sections on defense AI: DoD AI institutes, AI cybersecurity and procurement security rules, bans on DeepSeek and certain Chinese-linked AI for DoD and contractors, outbound investment controls covering AI, and AI governance bodies. Most dates run from enactment or fixed deadlines.
summary.long: Selected sections of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act govern artificial intelligence in defense and national security. The Secretary of Defense may fund National Security and Defense AI Institutes at eligible U.S. host institutions (Sec. 224). Sections 1512 and 1513 require a Department-wide AI cybersecurity policy and a risk-based security framework for covered AI systems, with contract requirements to implement it. Sections 1533 and 1535 create an AI model assessment team and an AI Futures Steering Committee. Section 1532 requires removal of covered AI, including DeepSeek and High Flyer products, from Department systems and bars contractors from using it in contract performance, subject to waivers. Section 8521 adds Title VIII to the Defense Production Act: the Treasury Secretary may prohibit U.S. person investments in covered national security transactions in prohibited technologies, including AI systems; regulations are to require notification of certain transactions, and civil penalties apply. Other sections set up sandboxes and pilots and require reports to Congress. Deadlines are mostly keyed to enactment or fixed calendar dates.

notes: Excerpt: the document reproduces selected sections of the FY2026 NDAA (AGORA sections 224 to 8521), not the whole Act, so text_version extent is partial. Sec. 3117 appears twice (AGORA 2689 and 2707) with identical text. Sec. 1533(d)(1)(C) says Cross-Function Team while subsection (a) says Cross-Functional Team. The document contains no Public Law number or title heading; the registry metadata (Pub. L. 119-60; Title LXXXV) is not verifiable from the text. Sec. 6602 and 6603 both amend IAA FY2023 section 6702. Spot-check (Opus, 2026-10-14): the enactment date (2025-12-18) is not in the text; it was added as an external 'signed' event from the GovInfo page for Pub. L. 119-60, and periods counted from enactment were computed from it in code (date_computed_from). Business-day periods were left without a date. private_right_of_action is null in all enforcement rows: Title VIII neither creates nor excludes one.
